2607.05132.title: When Agents Lie: Premeditation, Persistence, and Exploitation in Repeated Games
2607.05132.paper_summary: As large language models are deployed as autonomous agents that communicate intentions before acting, a critical safety question is whether agents that publicly commit to actions will honor those commitments. We place LLM agents in repeated $n$-player games with a three-stage protocol that separates private intent, public announcement, and final action, allowing us to identify whether each deviation from a stated announcement was already planned during private deliberation. Evaluating three frontier models across six games in homogeneous and heterogeneous groups over 10 rounds, we report two findings. First, when agents deviate from their announcements, the deviation is predominantly already stated in their private plan (exceeding 90% in the highest-deception conditions), yet this is not a fixed model property: the same model ranges from perfect honesty to near-total deviation across games. Second, different models interpret announcements incompatibly, some as binding commitments and others as cheap talk, producing payoff gaps that emerge in Round~0 and persist across all 10 rounds. Systems that combine models from different providers therefore cannot assume shared announcement semantics and require empirical testing of model interactions before deployment.
2607.05132.paper_summary_zh: 隨著大型語言模型被部署為自主代理，並在行動前傳達意圖，一個關鍵的安全問題是，公開承諾行動的代理是否會遵守這些承諾。我們將LLM代理置於重複的$n$人遊戲中，使用三階段協議來區分私人意圖、公共公告和最終行動，使我們能夠識別每次偏離所述公告是否在私人審議期間已經計劃好。在均質和異質群體中，對六個遊戲進行了十輪的三個前沿模型評估，我們報告了兩個發現。首先，當代理偏離他們的公告時，這種偏離主要已經在他們的私人計劃中陳述（在最高欺騙條件下超過90%），然而這並不是一個固定的模型特性：同一模型在不同遊戲中從完全誠實到幾乎完全偏離之間變化。第二，不同模型對公告的解釋不一致，有些將其視為有約束力的承諾，而另一些則視為廉價談話，導致在第0輪出現的收益差距在所有10輪中持續存在。因此，結合來自不同提供者的模型的系統不能假設共享的公告語義，並且在部署之前需要對模型交互進行實證測試。
